examples.en: On my trip to Japan I went to a karaoke place.
Karaoke is a machine for singing along to accompaniment.
I put a karaoke machine in the living room.
My friend likes karaoke, so we go often.
I liked the song I sang at karaoke.

examples.ko: 우리 동네에는 가라오케도 있고 노래방도 있어요.
examples.en: My neighborhood has both a karaoke bar and a noraebang.

explain: 한국에서 노래를 부르는 곳은 보통 '노래방'이라고 해요. '가라오케'는 일본에서 온 말이라 일본이나 외국의 시설을 이야기할 때 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: In Korea the usual word for a place to sing is '노래방'. '가라오케' came from Japan and is often used when talking about facilities in Japan or abroad.

examples.en: I saw a gorilla at the zoo.
The gorilla beat its chest.
Gorillas eat leaves.
The child walked like a gorilla.
I received a gorilla doll as a gift.
Gorillas also live together in family groups.

explain: '침팬지'와 같은 무리의 동물이에요. 몸은 침팬지보다 훨씬 크고, 꼬리가 없다는 점은 같아요.
explain_en: It belongs to the same group of animals as the 침팬지. A gorilla is much bigger than a chimpanzee, and both have no tail.

examples.ko: 두 번째 넘버를 부를 때 박수가 나왔어요.
examples.en: There was applause when they sang the second number.
A big number is written on the uniform.
I want to be number one.

examples.ko: 이 곡은 제가 제일 좋아하는 넘버예요.
examples.en: This is my favorite number.
We found the owner by the car number.
Musical numbers are easy to memorize.

explain: 일반적으로 숫자를 말할 때는 '번호'를 써요. '넘버'는 '넘버 원', '뮤지컬 넘버'처럼 외래어 표현 안에서 써요.
explain_en: For a plain number, use 'beonho'. 'Neombeo' appears inside loanword expressions like 'number one' and 'musical number'.

p.n: 넘버 sounds trendy or casual; 숫자 is the neutral Korean word.

examples.en: I received a ruby ring as a gift.
A ruby is a red gem.
A ruby is set in my grandmother's necklace.
The sunset was red like a ruby.
It sparkles more when I wipe the ruby with a cloth.
Which do you like, ruby or diamond?

explain: 탄생석 이야기를 할 때 '7월은 루비'처럼 말해요. 붉은 보석이라서 '루비색'이라고 하면 진한 붉은색을 가리켜요.
explain_en: In talk about birthstones, people say 'July is ruby'. Because it is a red gem, 'rubisaek' points to a deep red color.

examples.en: I learned how to greet people in Mongolian from a Mongolian friend.
They say Mongolian has a word order similar to Korean.
I'm majoring in Mongolian at university.

examples.ko: 몽골어 수업이 일주일에 두 번 있어요.
examples.en: There are Mongolian classes twice a week.
I'd like to try studying Mongolian later too.
A Mongolian interpreter attended the meeting.

explain: '몽골'에 '-어'를 붙여 언어 이름을 만들어요. 일본어, 영어, 러시아어처럼 나라 이름에 '-어'가 붙는 말이 많아요. '몽골어를 배우다', '몽골어로 말하다'처럼 '을/를'과 '(으)로'를 구별해서 써요.
explain_en: Adding '-어' to '몽골' gives the name of the language, like 일본어, 영어 and 러시아어. Use '을/를' for the object and '(으)로' for the language used, as in '몽골어를 배우다' and '몽골어로 말하다'.

examples.en: Yesterday's soccer match ended in a tie.
The two teams ended up in a tie.
It's a pity that this match was a tie.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 시즌에 무승부를 두 번 기록했어요.
examples.en: Our team drew twice this season.
Because the game was a tie, everyone applauded.
In a tie, each team gets one point.

explain: 경기가 같은 점수로 끝났을 때 쓰는 명사라서 '무승부가 되다', '무승부로 끝나다'처럼 써요. 같은 상황의 동사는 '비기다'예요. '승리', '패배'와 나란히 알아 두세요.
explain_en: It is a noun for a game that ends with equal scores, used as '무승부가 되다' or '무승부로 끝나다'. The verb for the same situation is '비기다'. Learn it together with '승리' (win) and '패배' (loss).

examples.en: The kids played shooting water guns in the park.
We had a water gun fight at the summer festival.
My younger sibling hit my back with a water gun.
Please fill the water gun with water.

examples.ko: 이 물총은 멀리까지 나가서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This water gun shoots far, so it's popular.

examples.ko: 물총이 고장 나서 물이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The water gun is broken, so no water comes out.

explain: '물총을 쏘다'처럼 '쏘다'와 함께 써요. 여름에 하는 놀이를 말할 때 '물총 싸움'이라는 말이 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It goes with '쏘다', as in '물총을 쏘다'. For the summer game, the phrase '물총 싸움' (water gun fight) comes up often.

examples.en: They scan the bar code at the checkout.
The bar code is torn, so it won't scan.

examples.ko: 바코드는 상품 정보를 기계로 읽게 해 줘요.
examples.en: A bar code lets a machine read product information.
Hold your phone camera up to the bar code.
You can also type in the bar code number.
A bar code also has to be clean to be read well.

explain: 마트 상품, 책, 택배 상자에서 볼 수 있어요. '바코드를 찍다', '바코드를 읽다'처럼 쓰고, 정사각형 모양의 'QR코드'와는 모양이 달라요.
explain_en: You can see it on supermarket goods, books, and delivery boxes. Say '바코드를 찍다' (scan) or '바코드를 읽다' (read). It looks different from a square 'QR코드'.

examples.ko: 비회원도 이 쿠폰을 쓸 수 있나요?
examples.en: Can nonmembers use this coupon too?

examples.ko: 비회원은 주문 조회 때 전화번호가 필요해요.
examples.en: Nonmembers need a phone number to look up an order.
If you buy as a nonmember, you don't earn points.

examples.ko: 이 도서관은 비회원에게 책을 빌려주지 않아요.
examples.en: This library doesn't lend books to nonmembers.
The nonmember price is higher than the member price.
I'm not a member, so I couldn't get the discount.

explain: 반의어는 '회원'이에요. 쇼핑몰에서 '비회원 구매', '비회원 주문'이라는 말을 자주 봐요. '비-'는 '아닌 사람/것'을 나타내서 '비공개', '비정규직'처럼 많은 말에 붙어요.
explain_en: The opposite is '회원' (member). You often see '비회원 구매' and '비회원 주문' on shopping sites. The prefix '비-' means 'not', and it appears in many words such as '비공개' and '비정규직'.

examples.en: I bought a file and a stapler at the stationery store.
The staples have already run out.
Staple the documents and submit them.

examples.ko: 스테이플러 좀 빌려 줄 수 있어요?
examples.en: Could you lend me a stapler?

examples.ko: 스테이플러가 고장 났는지 종이가 안 찍혀요.
examples.en: The stapler seems broken, because it won't staple the paper.
Where did you put the stapler that was on the desk?

explain: 종이를 찍는 것은 '찍다'를 써서 '스테이플러로 찍다'라고 해요. 한국에서는 '호치키스'라고 부르는 사람도 많아요.
explain_en: You use the verb '찍다' for stapling, as in '스테이플러로 찍다'. Many people in Korea also call it '호치키스'.

examples.en: The dance steps are too fast and hard.
I will practice from the basic steps first.

examples.ko: 스텝만 보면 쉬운데 따라 하기는 어려워요.
examples.en: The steps look easy on their own, but they are hard to follow.

examples.ko: 이 운동은 가볍게 스텝을 밟는 게 중요해요.
examples.en: In this exercise, stepping lightly is important.

examples.ko: 이 스텝을 천천히 다시 보여 주세요.
examples.en: Please show me this step again, slowly.

examples.ko: 가수의 화려한 스텝에 팬들이 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: Fans applauded the singer's flashy steps.

explain: 주로 춤·운동에서 발을 움직이는 동작에 써요. 일의 순서나 과정은 '단계'라고 해요. 영화·방송에서 일하는 사람은 '스태프'라서 '스텝'과 철자가 달라요.
explain_en: It mostly refers to footwork in dance and exercise. The order of a task is '단계'. Film and TV workers are '스태프' (staff), which is spelled differently from '스텝'.

examples.en: The pitcher threw a strike with the first pitch.

examples.ko: 스트라이크가 세 번 나오면 타자는 아웃이에요.
examples.en: When there are three strikes, the batter is out.

examples.ko: 오늘 볼링에서 연속으로 스트라이크 세 번을 쳤어요.
examples.en: Today in bowling I bowled three strikes in a row.
The umpire saw the ball and called a strike.
The last pitch was ruled a strike.
I hope it's a strike this time too.

explain: 야구에서는 심판이 스트라이크를 선언하고, 반대되는 말은 '볼'이에요. 볼링에서는 첫 공으로 핀을 모두 쓰러뜨릴 때 써요.
explain_en: In baseball the umpire calls a strike, and its opposite is a 볼. In bowling it is used when you knock down all the pins with the first ball.

examples.en: The bed springs are old and make noise.

examples.ko: 볼펜 안에는 작은 스프링이 꼭 들어 있어요.
examples.en: A small spring is always inside a ballpoint pen.
If you press the spring, it comes back up.

examples.ko: 이 소파는 스프링의 탄력이 좋아서 편해요.
examples.en: This sofa is comfortable because its springs are bouncy.

examples.ko: 스프링 노트는 한 장씩 뜯을 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can tear out a spring notebook one page at a time.
A door with a spring closes slowly.

explain: '용수철'이 같은 뜻의 우리말인데, 침대·소파·노트 같은 물건 이름에서는 '스프링'을 훨씬 많이 써요. 영어 spring에는 계절 뜻도 있지만 한국어에서 계절은 '봄'이라고 해요.
explain_en: '용수철' is the native Korean word with the same meaning, but in names of things like beds, sofas, and notebooks '스프링' is used far more often. English spring also means the season, but in Korean the season is '봄'.

examples.en: That look is a signal that he likes you.
Don't miss the signals your body sends.
A positive signal came from the company.
Signals show more clearly in actions than in words.
I react sensitively even to small signals.
I took those words as a signal of a breakup.

explain: 일상에서 신호등, 휴대폰 신호, 손짓 신호는 모두 '신호'라고 해요. '시그널'은 마음이나 분위기를 은근히 보여 주는 신호에 주로 써요.
explain_en: Traffic lights, phone signal, and hand signals are all '신호' in daily life. '시그널' is mainly used for subtle hints about feelings or mood.

examples.en: Today I wore matching black from top to bottom.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 저를 아래위로 쳐다봐서 불편했어요.
examples.en: That person looked me up and down, and it made me uncomfortable.
The child bobs their head up and down happily.
You open and close the window by moving it up and down.

examples.ko: 아래위로 흔들리는 버스 안에서 책을 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a book on a bus that was bouncing up and down.

examples.ko: 아래위가 똑같은 옷을 입으면 쌍둥이 같아요.
examples.en: If you wear the same top and bottom, you look like twins.

explain: '위아래'와 같은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요. 옷 이야기에서는 윗옷과 아래옷을 함께 가리킬 때가 많아요.
explain_en: It can be used with the same meaning as '위아래'. When talking about clothes, it often refers to the top and bottom together.

examples.ko: 차가 오자 도로 한가운데 안전지대로 피했어요.
examples.en: When a car came, I moved to the safety zone in the middle of the road.
I waited in the safety zone in front of the bus stop.
These days nowhere is a completely safe zone.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 홍수 걱정이 없는 안전지대예요.
examples.en: This area is a safe zone where there is no worry about floods.

examples.ko: 길 가운데 안전지대에 서서 신호를 기다렸어요.
examples.en: I stood on the safety island in the middle of the road and waited for the signal.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 와도 우리 마을은 안전지대예요.
examples.en: Even when it rains a lot, our village is a safe zone.

explain: 도로 가운데 사람이 잠시 피해 서 있는 구역이라는 실제 장소도 가리키고, 위험이 없는 곳이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 비유로 쓸 때는 '어디도 안전지대가 아니다'처럼 부정문에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It can mean an actual spot in the middle of a road where people can stand safely, and it is also widely used figuratively for a place free of danger. In the figurative sense it often appears in negatives like '어디도 안전지대가 아니다' (nowhere is safe).

examples.en: He is a patriot who loves his country.
I read the story of a patriot in a book.
It is a class where we learn about patriots in history.
I remember the patriot who took part in the independence movement.
Being called a patriot is a great honor.

examples.ko: 그 애국자는 어려운 때에도 나라를 떠나지 않았어요.
examples.en: That patriot did not leave the country even in hard times.

explain: 나라를 위해 크게 힘쓴 사람에게 존경을 담아 써요. 일상에서 자기를 가리켜 '저는 애국자예요'라고 하면 조금 거창하게 들려요. '애국지사'는 특히 독립을 위해 싸운 분들께 써요.
explain_en: It is used with respect for someone who devoted themselves to the nation. Saying '저는 애국자예요' about yourself in daily life sounds a bit grand. '애국지사' is used especially for those who fought for independence.

examples.en: This monitor is 27 inches.
Some TVs are over 55 inches.
My laptop is only 15 inches.
I bought the 32-inch one because the screen is bigger.
One inch is about 2.5 centimeters.
What size tablet, in inches, do you want to buy?

explain: TV나 모니터, 휴대폰 화면 크기는 센티미터가 아니라 '인치'로 말해요. '27인치'처럼 숫자 뒤에 붙여 써도 되고 띄어 써도 돼요.
explain_en: Screen sizes of TVs, monitors, and phones are given in 인치, not centimeters. It can be written attached to the number or with a space, as in 27인치 or 27 인치.
